items.Q7: applicable and met. Secret search over the change and the page files (self_check S1): no match that is a secret. The invite code is 16 random bytes (128 bits), shown once in the answer of N4, stored only as HMAC-SHA256(pepper, 'invite\0'+code) (org-store.js:59, keys.js label invite); probe: the stored code_hash equals my own HMAC and the code appears in no row, audit row or log line, and the log route is the pattern /api/invites/:code, not the path. No e-mail, name, address or code in any audit row or log line after the whole probe (sp8: invite create and accept, request and deletion, 20 project writes). The consent record holds the digest, the language and the time only.
items.Q8: applicable and met. The organisation of a tenant request comes only from the session's membership (readSession), never from the body, the path or the query: probe, a body key org_id, orgId, organisation or created_by on N12 -> 400 bad_body; ?org_id= ignored; a user without a membership -> uniform 404 (pipeline step 9a). Other organisations' objects: N13 and N14 for a foreign project answer the same 404 as a missing one, byte-equal in body and headers, and a viewer on a foreign project gets that 404 (the object is checked before the role, planIdeaEdit lines 144-151), no version written. Roles: viewer 403 on create and on edit of an own project with nothing written; member, org_admin, org_owner write. RLS enabled and forced on projects, idea_versions, org_members, invites, audit_log, orgs; tenant A cannot read, insert into, update or delete B's rows (42501 or 0 rows), cannot add a version that points into B's project (composite foreign key); the grants of sai_app equal the design table exactly; sai_preview, sai_app_login and PUBLIC hold nothing on the new tables. Admin routes N4-N10: anonymous and an org_owner get the uniform 404 byte-equal to an unknown path; N4 and N6 need a re-auth token of their own purpose (owner_identity, user_delete), a token of another purpose -> 403; N8 writes exactly one admin_read row (actor admin, the project's organisation, target the project) per call and none for a miss.
items.Q9: applicable and met. No .query or .exec with a template literal or concatenation in app/server, app/api, app/scripts; every statement is a constant in org-store.js, project-store.js, audit-store.js or auth-store.js with bound parameters; the text app.purge_org stands only in project-store.js:235,240 and the migration; no statement deletes or updates idea_versions or projects outside project-store.js (grep, self_check S2).
items.Q10: applicable and met. The new refusals are named codes in the closed list; a failure inside an accept after the claim rolls the whole transaction back: probe, a forced failure at the audit insert -> 5xx, no user, consent, organisation or membership, the invite is NOT spent. A plan or handler that throws rolls back its audit row and its action together (probe). A TypeError of a bad plan answers exactly {"error":"server_error"}. Hostile input: a 60 KB body -> 413, an 8000-character idea with a zero-width sign at its end -> 400 in 3 ms, a 60k-deep JSON -> 400 bad_json, a 5000-character password on accept -> 400 with no scrypt; a markup title is stored and returned as JSON text with nosniff.
items.Q11: not applicable: no address set by a client or user is called by the server.
items.invite_token: met. Entropy 128 bits (crypto.randomBytes(16), orgs.js:124). Stored as HMAC only. One-time use under concurrency: claimInvite is one conditional UPDATE ... where used_at is null and expires_at > now returning id, after every check and after the password hash, so no lock is held through scrypt; probe: 4 parallel accepts of one code -> exactly one 200 and three 404 (PGlite serialises, so the logic only: the row lock under Postgres is to be proved by the pg job). A failure after the claim leaves the invite unspent. Expiry exactly 7 days -> 404. An unknown, malformed, used and expired code, and a wrong e-mail, all answer the same 404 body and headers (byte-equal to each other; for GET also equal to an unknown /api path); a refusal depending on the body is thrown before the invite is read, so it reveals nothing about a code. Address limits: the 11th accept and the 61st view from one address -> 429.
items.acceptance_atomic: met. User, consent record, membership (a new customer organisation first, ai_allowed false, the user its org_owner), the spent invite, the audit row invite.accept (actor user, details {role, owner_identity} only) and the session are written in the one request transaction; probe: counts after a success are 1 user, 1 consent, 1 organisation, org_owner membership, invite used with used_by; a unique violation on the e-mail is mapped to account_exists and rolls back.
items.G7_gate: met. The gate is the constant PERSONAL_DATA_GATE = 'owner_only' in app/server/services/orgs.js:56; the app takes another value only from deps.auth.personalDataGate (tests), no environment variable or setting. Checked at creation (N4: an invite for a non-owner identity -> 403 personal_data_gate, nothing stored) and again at acceptance (a planted non-owner invite row -> 403 personal_data_gate, no user created, the invite unspent). The owner organisation takes only owner identities (N4 owner_identity_required; the 0002 trigger; the new users trigger refuses clearing the flag of an owner-org member: P0001). Registration mode: closed and any other value -> 403 registration_closed, missing, invite and open accept (fail closed).
items.consent: met. Five sentences in the texts module; the page joins them with one space and hashes with Web Crypto, the server hashes its own copy with the same function (shared/consent.js) and compares; a false consent -> 400 consent_required; a stale digest, the digest of another language, and a language the server holds no complete text for (the production texts without kk, probed with planted texts) -> 400 consent_stale, nothing created; consent_langs lists the languages the server can verify. The box is not pre-ticked (no checked attribute) and a consent as a string or a number -> bad_body. Stored digest equals the server's digest of the ru text.
items.deletion: met with the finding F1. N3 needs the password (a wrong one -> 401, counted as a re-auth failure, nothing stored); a second request while one is open stores nothing and answers the first time; the platform admin -> 403 and nothing stored. N6 needs a user_delete re-auth token, refuses the platform admin (403), a non-uuid and an already deleted user (404). Probe after a deletion: e-mail, normalised e-mail and name are placeholders, the password hash is DELETED_HASH (never verifies), status deleted, TOTP fields cleared; sessions, re-auth tokens, reset codes and the membership are gone; the e-mail of the invite he used is replaced; the old session is dead; a login with the old e-mail and with the placeholder e-mail answers like an unknown e-mail (byte-equal, one scrypt); the consent digest stays (no personal value); the open request is closed. The projects of an organisation that still has a member stay; when the last member is deleted the organisation's idea versions and projects are purged (the organisation row stays); app.purge_org is empty outside the purge. Audit rows hold no e-mail or name. The owner organisation cannot lose its last member (the admin cannot be deleted); see F4.
items.purge_protocol: met, residual named by the design (4.2.3). Only purgeOrg (project-store.js:232-246) sets app.purge_org, refuses unless app.role is platform (TypeError, no statement), sets it, deletes the versions, clears it, deletes the projects; the trigger fires for every role: probe, as the owner UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE of idea_versions -> P0001; as sai_app (no UPDATE grant) refused; a platform transaction that set the purge setting of ANOTHER organisation cannot delete this one's versions (P0001). Residual, as the design says: a connection that can run its own SQL as sai_app can set the setting for its own organisation (probe INFO: deleted its own org's versions); the app has no statement that does so (grep) and every statement is a constant of a store file.
items.tenant_pipeline: met. Step 9a (auth-mw.js:229-264): the plan runs on the platform settings of the request transaction, the audit entry is built from the session (organisation, actor kind, actor, address) and exactly four keys are copied from the plan after a check that it has exactly action, targetKind, targetId, details (appendAudit then validates the action and the closed details keys); then switchToTenant; then the handler. Probes: a plan with an extra orgId, actorKind or ip key, a missing details key, an action outside the list used with a PII detail key, and a detail key outside the closed list -> 500 server_error, no audit row; a plan with audit null runs the handler with no row; a handler that fails after the audit row rolls both back (the project and the audit row); the statement order of a request is set role and settings (platform), the plan, insert into audit_log, then the second settings statement (tenant), then the handler (planRole 'platform', handlerRole 'tenant', org = the session's); withPlan on a non-tenant row throws at table build. Every project audit row carries the session's organisation and actor and the address HMAC, with details {stage} or {version} only.
items.versions: met. The plan locks the project row (select ... for update with the organisation filter) and reads max(version)+1 in the same transaction; unique (project_id, version) is the backstop; the check (version = 1) = (reason is null) and the composite foreign key hold in the database. Probe: edits give 2, 3; five parallel edits give 1..8 with no gap or duplicate (logic only under PGlite; the lock under Postgres is for the pg job); an empty reason or text -> bad_body. The 21st project of a user in 24 h -> 429 with Retry-After and nothing stored; the count of a refused request rolls back; another user's quota is separate.
items.word_list_exception: met. stripDeletionTerm removes the first occurrence of the one phrase per language and only for the five consent keys (check-public.js); a value with the phrase twice, or a day form beside it, or a day form without it, is still found; a fuzz of 4000 random token strings never hid a day form outside the first phrase and never added a finding; a language outside ru, kk, en throws RangeError; the key list of word-lists.js equals the literal list of shared/consent.js.
items.grants_sql: met. The new blocks are static and one per table (projects select, insert, update, delete; idea_versions select, insert, delete; deletion_requests select, insert, update; user_consents select, insert); org_members gains delete and invites gains delete; the probe compares information_schema with the design table and finds no difference; no TRUNCATE, no UPDATE on idea_versions, no DELETE on users, orgs or audit_log.
items.xss: met. See the surface map: every dynamic text of the ten pages and their scripts goes through textContent or el({text}); a markup title and idea come back as JSON text with nosniff and are shown as text; the invite page reads the code from the fragment and clears it with history.replaceState; the CSP of the app is unchanged.

No CI run of e656e6c exists yet (gh run list shows none for it); the pg and migration-rehearsal jobs must prove them. findings.place: app/server/services/orgs.js:364-400 (deleteAccount) with app/server/db/org-store.js:124-129 (scrubInviteEmails: 'update invites set email_norm = $2 where used_by = $1'); acceptInvite at orgs.js:230
findings.item: decisions/0100 items 1 and 5 (an account and its data are deleted); REQ-116 criterion 6
findings.severity: MEDIUM, not blocking (production holds only owner identities while the gate is owner_only; fix before the gate is flipped to «б»)
findings.what: Deletion scrubs only the invites the user USED. An unused invite for the same e-mail (the admin made two, or an earlier one was never used) keeps the e-mail in clear in invites.email_norm until 30 days after its expiry, and it is still valid: probe sp10, after the deletion of an account made from invite 1, invite 2 for the same address still holds the e-mail, can still be viewed (200) and still creates a NEW account for the old address (200).
findings.fix: In deleteAccount read the target's email_norm before anonymiseUser (lockUserForDelete already selects the row; add the column) and run one more constant statement in org-store.js, e.g. 'delete from invites where used_at is null and email_norm = $1', before the scrub; and in acceptInvite after the claim (orgs.js:230) delete the other unused invites of that e-mail. Add the case to the deletion tests (DEL: a second unused invite for the address is gone after the deletion).

findings.item: Q8 (which fields go to the customer is the server's decision)
findings.what: N13 gives every member of an organisation the author's user id and name of each version, so a customer sees the platform admin's user id and display name on versions the admin edited (probe: the author name is the admin's). The design lists it, and the id gives no capability (every admin route needs the admin's own session), but it is more than the customer needs.
findings.fix: For a version whose author is the platform admin return {name: 'Sai', admin: true} without the id (the card for the admin keeps the real author), or return only a role mark; adjust the N13 shape in the design and test.

findings.item: decisions/0100 'never log e-mails'; audit of personal-data reads
findings.what: N8 (the project card) writes an admin_read audit row, but N5 (the list of deletion requests with the requester's name and e-mail) reads personal data and writes none. Only the admin can call it and it needs the session, so it is not a leak; it is an inconsistency in the trail.
findings.fix: Either write one admin_read-style row per call of N5 (a new closed action) or record in the design that the list is not audited.

findings.item: defence in depth (REQ-117 criterion 9, the owner-organisation guard)
findings.what: The purge of an organisation's projects runs when its member count reaches 0, with no check on the organisation's kind. It cannot reach the owner organisation today, because the platform admin is its permanent member and cannot be deleted (N6 refuses him; the users trigger refuses clearing his flag), but nothing in the purge says so.
findings.fix: Skip the purge when the organisation's kind is 'owner' (readOrgKind or the kind already read by orgsOfUser), with a test that a planted owner organisation with no member keeps its projects.

issues.text: F1-F4 are not blocking. F1 is the one to fix in this run (a few lines, and it must be fixed before the G7 gate is flipped to «б»); F2-F4 may become ISS entries. ORCH decides whether CODE-FIXER takes them.

Row-lock races (the invite claim, the version number) and RLS, the purge trigger and grants on real Postgres 17 are proven here by reading and PGlite only; the pg and migration-rehearsal jobs on GitHub must prove them. No CI run of e656e6c exists yet.

For REVIEWER (not a verdict item): the accept route returns the stored e-mail only through the admin N5 list; the invite link of N4 is returned in the body and shown once by the page, as designed; the consent sentence says the data is kept until the account is deleted, while the audit chain and the consent digest outlive it (no personal value), which the sentence does not claim to cover.
